notes: The circuit image draws the I2C bus lines and the two 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors as plain lines with no breadboard. The manual lists mini breadboards and jumper wires, so I put the SDA bus (column 5t), the SCL bus (column 8t) and the 3.3 V rail (tp) on one breadboard. The exact hole positions are my own choice.
I used one breadboard, not the two mini breadboards in the parts list, because the image shows no board layout.

Wiring follows the image. A4 (SDA, yellow) of both boards joins one bus, and A5 (SCL, teal) of both boards joins another. Each bus has a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to the reader's 3V pin. GND of the two boards is joined directly.
Only the reader's 3V pin is wired to the pull-ups. The writer's 3V pin is not connected.
The parts list says 10 jumper wires, but only 6 are needed for the drawn circuit.
Both boards are powered and serial-connected through USB cables to a computer. The computer is not in the catalogue, so it is not modelled and the USB cables have no ports.
The Nano 33 IoT is a new part type. Its built-in LED (LED_BUILTIN) is internal to the board, so I did not model it separately.
The image labels the supply pin '3V'. I mapped it to port 3.3V.
